analysis.investment_thesis: Alembic scores poorly on both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield of ~6.1% (EBIT ₹1,008 Cr / EV ~₹16,600 Cr) barely clears the minimum, while ROIC of ~13-15% falls well short of the 20%+ threshold for a "good" business. With FCF turning sharply negative in FY2025 (-₹466 Cr) and a 9-year net profit CAGR of -2.3%, this is a business that has consumed capital without compounding returns.
key_strengths: High gross margins (71.5%) indicate strong product-level economics in its pharmaceutical portfolio.
Promoter holding at 69.74% with low D/E of 0.28 (pre-2025) signals owner-operated discipline.
Revenue has grown from ₹3,166 Cr to ₹6,672 Cr over 9 years — the top line is real.
key_risks: EBITDA has gone nowhere in 9 years (₹1,079 Cr in 2016 → ₹1,052 Cr in 2025), meaning all revenue growth has been absorbed by costs.
FY2025 OCF collapsed to ₹88 Cr from ₹803 Cr in FY2024 — a severe red flag on earnings quality.
Borrowings surged from ₹513 Cr to ₹1,489 Cr in FY2025 while FCF is negative — balance sheet is deteriorating fast.
red_flags: FY2025 Free Cash Flow: -₹466 Cr — the company burned cash despite reporting ₹582 Cr net profit.
Finance costs rose from ₹5 Cr (2016) to ₹79 Cr (2025), a 35.9% CAGR — debt addiction is worsening.
Net profit 9-year CAGR is -2.3% — a company trading at 23x P/E with shrinking earnings is expensive, not cheap.
EBITDA peaked at ₹1,663 Cr in FY2021 and has contracted since — the margin expansion story reversed.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EV = Market Cap (₹15,425 Cr) + Net Debt (₹1,258 - ₹83 = ₹1,175 Cr) ≈ ₹16,600 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income) FY2025 = ₹1,008 Cr. Earnings Yield = 6.1% — barely at the minimum I'd consider (need >12% to be interesting). Invested Capital = Equity (₹5,319) + Debt (₹1,258) - Cash (₹83) ≈ ₹6,494 Cr. ROIC = ₹1,008/₹6,494 = 15.5% — confirmed by the given ROCE of 13%. Neither metric clears my bar. On the Magic Formula ranking, this company would sit in the bottom half of a screened universe.

What concerns me more is the trajectory. The capex supercycle (CWIP peaked at ₹2,304 Cr in FY2022) was supposed to drive earnings. Instead, EBITDA in FY2025 (₹1,052 Cr) is essentially identical to FY2016 (₹1,079 Cr) — nine years of investment for zero EBITDA growth. The FY2025 OCF implosion to ₹88 Cr (from ₹1,463 Cr in FY2021) combined with fresh borrowings of nearly ₹1B suggests working capital stress or one-time cash drains. At 23x earnings with this capital efficiency and FCF track record, the stock is not cheap enough to compensate for the quality deficit.
